title: New urine culture order
objectives: Collect a clean-catch urine specimen correctly and label it at the bedside
Recognize when a result needs same-shift escalation rather than routine follow-up
Document a lab result with the provider notification it triggered
opening: You are reviewing your 1400 task list. The provider ordered a urinalysis with reflex culture this morning after Mrs. Vance reported burning with urination overnight. The order has been sitting unstarted since 0730. She is alert, mildly uncomfortable, and asks when someone is going to 'deal with the bathroom thing.'

actions.label: Review the order and her recent history first
actions.detail: Check for prior UTIs and current antibiotic allergies before collecting.
actions.response: Order confirms UA with reflex culture and sensitivity. Chart shows two UTIs in the past year, both treated with nitrofurantoin. Allergy list confirms sulfa, not nitrofurantoin or beta-lactams — relevant if this comes back positive and needs treatment.

actions.label: Hand her a cup and ask her to go whenever
actions.detail: She's able to get up on her own.
actions.response: A random-void specimen risks contamination from perineal skin flora, which can produce a false-positive culture and an unnecessary antibiotic course. For a culture, a clean-catch technique matters — a few minutes of instruction now saves a repeat collection later.

actions.label: Instruct and assist with clean-catch technique
actions.detail: Cleanse front to back, catch midstream.
actions.response: She is able to follow the steps with the peri-wipes provided. Specimen obtained: cloudy, strong odor, approximately 40 mL.

actions.label: Label at the bedside and send to the lab
actions.detail: Two identifiers, date, and time on the label before it leaves the room.
actions.response: Specimen labeled with name, MRN, and collection time at bedside, then sent via tube system. Lab confirms receipt.

actions.label: Wait for the full 48-hour culture before doing anything else
actions.detail: The culture takes two days to result anyway.
actions.response: The rapid UA component results in under an hour and can already show a strong signal for infection — nitrites, leukocyte esterase, WBCs — well before the culture confirms an organism. Waiting on the culture alone means missing findings that change her care today.

actions.label: Check the UA result once it posts
actions.detail: Rapid component usually results within the hour.
actions.response: UA positive: leukocyte esterase large, nitrites positive, WBC 45/hpf, few bacteria. Consistent with UTI. Culture and sensitivity still pending, expected in 48 hours.
actions.criticalWhy: A positive UA in a patient with CKD stage 3 and a sulfa allergy needs the provider looped in before empiric treatment is chosen — not every antibiotic is safe for her kidneys.

actions.label: Notify the provider of the positive UA
actions.detail: Report the result and her relevant history.
actions.response: Dr. Patel reviews the result and her CKD stage and prior nitrofurantoin tolerance. New order: start nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID pending culture, encourage oral fluids, repeat BMP in the morning to trend renal function.

actions.label: Start the new antibiotic and encourage fluids
actions.detail: First dose now, water at bedside.
actions.response: First dose of nitrofurantoin given with food to reduce GI upset, per pharmacy note. Water pitcher filled and placed within reach. She states she understands to finish the full course.

actions.label: Hold off telling her anything until the culture confirms it
actions.detail: No sense worrying her over a preliminary result.
actions.response: The UA result and the new medication are being started now — she is entitled to know what she is being given and why, even while confirmatory results are pending. Keeping a patient in the dark about her own treatment is not protecting her.

hints: The order has two parts, and one of them results much faster than the other.
Her allergy list and her kidney history both matter before any antibiotic gets picked.
A random-void specimen and a clean-catch specimen are not interchangeable for a culture.

documentation.prompt: Write your nursing note covering the specimen collection through the new medication.
documentation.placeholder: Begin with the time and the order you were acting on...

requirements.label: What was ordered and why (symptom prompting it)
requirements.why: Shows the specimen wasn't collected at random — there was a clinical reason.

requirements.label: Clean-catch technique used
requirements.why: Documents the specimen is valid for culture, not just a random void.

requirements.label: UA result, with the specific findings
requirements.why: The actual values, not just 'UA was positive.'

requirements.label: Culture and sensitivity still pending
requirements.why: So the next shift knows to watch for that result and doesn't assume treatment is already confirmed.

requirements.label: Provider notified, with time and new orders
requirements.why: Times and names — this is what makes the escalation verifiable.

requirements.label: Allergy status considered in medication choice
requirements.why: Shows the medication choice wasn't just whatever was ordered — it was checked against her allergy list.

requirements.label: New medication given, with time and dose
requirements.why: The actual first dose administration needs a timestamp like any medication.

requirements.label: Patient education on the new medication
requirements.why: Finishing an antibiotic course matters, and documenting teaching protects both her and you.

documentation.modelNote:
1402 — Reviewing order for UA with reflex culture, placed 0730 for dysuria overnight. Chart reviewed: history of recurrent UTIs, prior treatment with nitrofurantoin without issue, sulfa allergy noted. CKD stage 3.

1407 — Clean-catch specimen obtained with patient assistance and instruction, cloudy with strong odor, approximately 40 mL. Labeled at bedside with two identifiers and sent to lab via tube system.

1425 — UA result reviewed: leukocyte esterase large, nitrites positive, WBC 45/hpf, few bacteria. Culture and sensitivity pending, results expected in 48 hours.

1429 — Dr. Patel notified of positive UA and patient's CKD/allergy history. New order received: nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID pending culture, encourage oral fluids, repeat BMP in AM.

1432 — First dose nitrofurantoin 100 mg given with food. Patient educated on completing full course and reporting any rash or GI upset. Water pitcher filled, encouraged to increase oral intake. Patient verbalizes understanding. Will monitor for symptom improvement and follow up on culture result when available.
pitfalls: Writing 'UA sent' with no result documented once it posts — the loop has to close.
Skipping the specific UA values and just writing 'positive for infection.'
Forgetting to note the allergy check before a new antibiotic is given.
Leaving out that the culture is still pending — the next shift needs to know to watch for it.
